content.text: Polysaccharide Iron Complex: Administration: 50mg, 50mg elemental Fe/tab, 1-2/day
Clin Use: IDA 1st-line (ferrous gluconate, sulfate, fumarate, or ferric maltol)
better absorbed in mildly acidic medium → take w/ vit C (orange juice or ascorbic acid tab) on empty stomach; Ca, phosphates, phytates + tannates (ex, milk) bind Fe → ⇣absorb
Monitor: repeat Hgb after 2wks (rises slowly); every-other-day dosing effective
Class: chelated Fe -chem altered -> thru digestive system w.o breaking
Bisglicinato ferroso quelatom, Bis-glycino iron II, Bisglycino-iron (II) chelate, Eisen(II)-bisglycinat,Ferrous glycinate, Iron glycinate
: replaces Fe, found in hgb, myoglobin, and other enzymes; allows the transportation of O2 via hgb
: MC product for oral replace therapy
SE: constipation, darkens stool, nausea, epigastric pain
BBW: accidental OD of iron-containing prod = a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children <6yo – keep product out of reach of children
: delivers Fe as ferritin; dissociates upon uptake from the GI tract allowing Fe and maltol to be absorbed separately
: Fe replace product for the tx of Fe deficiency in adults
: hemochromatosis & other Fe overload syndromes; pts requiring repeated blood transfusions
: flatulence, diarrhea, constipation, discolored feces, abd pain/discomfort/distention
: ⍉use if IBD flare = present, danger of iron-overload in children

content.text: Administration: Oral ->⍉tol -> dilute inj solution w SW for inj oral or parenteral
Parenteral (IV, subcut, deep IM) -> only if oral ⍉feasible
Monitoring:      -    CBC             -     Serum folate           -    Serum vit B12
MOA: anti-inflam via multi actions on several types of WBCs
Carpal tunnel syndrome: local inj (or oral)
Plantar fasciitis: inj ⍉1st-line (⇡risk of fascia rupture + fat pad atrophy) → short-term only; topical: limited evidence
▪︎OA: intra-articular inj relieves joint pain for several wks; ≤4x/yr per joint
▪︎AS: generally avoid (minimal impact; may worsen osteopenia)
Pericarditis: refractory/recurrent only; ⍉routine early (⇡recurrence); ⍉after MI (impairs myocardial healing)
▪︎Alopecia areata: intralesional corticosteroid (triamcinolone q4–6 wks); topical corticosteroid (fluocinolone acetonide cream BID)
▪︎Pityriasis rosea: may improve lesions + pruritus but ⍉routine (lack of evidence; relapse concern)
Nasal polyps + allergic rhinitis: short course
Lichen planus: topical or oral steroids (severity-dependent)
Aphthous stomatitis: complex/refractory (oral prednisone x4-7 days)
▪︎Bacterial meningitis: dexamethasone w/ abx (adjunct) → ⇣inflam + prevent neuro comps (eg hearing loss)
▪︎Sarcoidosis: tx of choice (prednisone, typically up to 6mo b4 taper)
▪︎Berylliosis: symptomatic + abnl PFTs (ex, prednisone); most need lifelong low-dose
▪︎Primary AI (Addison): lifelong replacement (prednisone, hydrocortisone, dexamethasone) + mineralocorticoid (fludrocortisone)
▪︎Cushing dz postop: empiric hydrocortisone for cortisol withdrawal Sx, taper slowly
▪︎ITP: life-threatening bleed → IV methylprednisolone; ⍉rapid plt rise needed → PO dexamethasone or prednisone
▪︎GPA: systemic GC + MTX (limited dz); + cyclophosphamide (more severe dz)
↑bone catabolism or antagonize vit D driven Ca absorb
Stim gastric acid & pepsin prod -> take w food
Admin: IV for critically ill, PO, rectal
Bell palsy: 60–80 mg/day x1 wk; ideally start w.in first 3 days of onset
Giant cell arteritis: high-dose prednisone PO (IV methylprednisolone if vision loss)
SLE: short-term prednisone initially → taper once HCQ or chloroquine takes effect
Admin: IV for critically ill, PO, rectal

: cortisol, as well as other steroid hormones, binds to intracell receptors – the steroid-receptor complex enters the nucleus and acts as a transcription factor to turn on certain genes, causing synth of specific proteins which are responsible for its physiological actions
Increases BG, increases protein catabolism from musc/bone, antagonist of insulin
Inhibits #/activity of cells involved in inflam response
Inhibits his release from mast cells
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/H2O retention, potassium loss
•Replace therapy: AI (Addison's dz) and CAH (defects in enzymes for steroid hormone synth)
•Dexamethasone suppression test (DST): dx of Cushing’s syndrome
•Tx of chronic inflam diseases:  RA, UC, asthma, SLE, eye and skin inflam
•Tx of allergic rxns: drug, serum, and transfusion rxns
•IS: prev of graft reject after transplantation
